details:
Symptom. While VRChat runs, the whole Windows desktop and all keyboard and mouse input freeze. The VRChat window stops rendering (the Steam overlay logs "The game hasn't rendered a frame from us in over 10 seconds"). Some kernel work carries on for a few minutes (SteamVR tracking keeps logging). The only ways out are the power button or a manual crash dump. This has happened at least 6 times since 2026-10-29. On 2026-11-10 at 00:13 local time I took a full kernel dump with the keyboard crash combo (bugcheck 0xE2), about 66 s after the freeze began.

System.

Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build 26200.9711. Hyper-V/VBS (HVCI) is on.

Intel i9-14900K, 96 GB RAM, Z790 board.

RTX 5090, driver 610.88 (nvlddmkm.sys timestamp 2026-07-21).

EasyAntiCheat_EOS.sys, timestamp 2026-10-21 19:17:58 (6AD95636).

VRChat build 2026.4.1p2-1938-565822d00a-Release, running with SteamVR.

What the dump shows (observed).

30 of 32 CPUs are idle. No DPCs are pending and no spinlocks are held. The GPU driver's threads and DPCs are still running. So this is a lock wait, not a CPU, GPU or USB hang.

An EasyAntiCheat_EOS System thread has been in NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemHandleInformation) for 4213 ticks (65.8 s). It is inside ExpSnapShotHandleTables, which means it holds the handle-table-list lock shared. It is blocked in PsLookupProcessByProcessId, waiting on the lock of one process. That process (EPROCESS ffff92825f170080) is not on the active process list.

About 10 more EAC threads, one of them running inside a bash.exe process, are queued for the same snapshot.

Short-lived processes that are exiting (sed.exe, sh.exe, sleep.exe) have been blocked for 4215 ticks in ObKillProcess → ExpRemoveHandleTable, waiting for that lock exclusively.

A git.exe thread creating a process has been blocked for 4215 ticks in PspInsertProcess → PspLockProcessListExclusive.

88 threads wait in PspLockProcessListExclusive, mostly through PsGetSessionById. They include csrss, dwm, lsass, VRChat and vrcompositor.

The win32k USER lock has 57 exclusive and 15 shared waiters, among them dwm, csrss, explorer and VRChat. Its owner is a SteamVR overlay thread inside NtUserSendInput → NtUpdateWnfStateData → PsGetSessionById, which is itself waiting for the process-list lock. This is why the desktop and input froze.

EAC thread (System), Ticks 4213:

  nt!ExfAcquireReleasePushLockExclusive+0x28

  nt!PsLookupProcessByProcessId+0x2aa

  nt!ExpSnapShotHandleTables+0x103

  nt!ObGetHandleInformation+0x3a

  nt!ExpQuerySystemInformation+0x929

  nt!NtQuerySystemInformation+0x5d

  EasyAntiCheat_EOS+0x10c8d2 / +0x3ae031 / +0x10c77b

Exiting sed.exe, Ticks 4215:

  nt!ExfAcquirePushLockExclusiveEx+0x195

  nt!ExpRemoveHandleTable+0x5e

  nt!ExDestroyHandleTable+0xe

  nt!ObKillProcess+0x4c

  nt!PspRundownSingleProcess+0xba

git.exe creating a process, Ticks 4215:

  nt!PspLockProcessListExclusive+0x44

  nt!PspInsertProcess+0xa6

  nt!NtCreateUserProcess+0xf72

USER lock owner (SteamVR overlay):

  nt!PspLockProcessListExclusive+0x44

  nt!PsGetSessionById+0x31

  nt!ExpNtUpdateWnfStateData+0x2c4

  win32kbase!CInputGlobals::UpdateInputGlobals+0x1b7

  win32kfull!NtUserSendInput+0x2a5

Conditions. Developer tools were creating and ending many short-lived processes (bash, sed, sleep, git) at the same time as VRChat was running.

Inferred, not proven. These look like the parts of a deadlock between EAC's kernel-mode handle snapshot and process creation or exit. EAC holds the handle-table-list lock and waits on a process that is half-created or exiting. That process, or the process-list lock, is waiting for the handle-table-list lock. The dump does not show which thread holds the process-list push lock, because push locks don't record their owner.

I can share the full kernel dump (13.8 GB) privately on request.
title: Desktop and input freeze while VRChat runs: kernel dump shows EasyAntiCheat_EOS stuck in a handle snapshot
